articles.title: Lula's comeback bid vs Bolsonaro's son: Brazil votes in high-stakes run-off
articles.summary: Brazilian voters are set to cast their ballots on Sunday in a tightly contested presidential run-off between incumbent left-wing leader Luiz Inácio Lula
articles.body: Brazilian voters are set to cast their ballots on Sunday in a tightly contested presidential run-off between incumbent left-wing leader Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, and right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro, 45.Lula is seeking a fourth, non-consecutive term as president, while Bolsonaro, the son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, is attempting to secure the top office. His father is serving a 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election, according to BBC report.Bolsonaro enters the final round with momentum after finishing ahead of Lula in the first round of voting on October 4. US President Donald Trump described that result as a “very big” victory.No candidate who has finished behind their rival in the first round has ever managed to overturn the deficit and win Brazil's presidential run-off.Bolsonaro supporters call for changeSupporters of Flávio Bolsonaro expressed confidence at his final campaign rallies, backing his promises to tackle organised crime through tougher measures, reduce taxes and cut public spending.On the eve of the election, Bolsonaro campaigned in Belo Horizonte, the capital of Minas Gerais. The state has been considered crucial for presidential candidates since the 1980s.“The time is almost here,” Bolsonaro said in a video posted on social media.“There are only a few hours left before we shape the future of our nation for the next 30 or 40 years,” he added.He has also pledged to secure the release of his father, who is serving his sentence under house arrest because of health problems.In Rio de Janeiro's Barra de Tijuca neighbourhood, where Jair Bolsonaro owns a home, supporters gathered wearing Brazil's national colours to demonstrate their backing for the senator.One supporter told BBC News that the country needed a change in leadership and described Flávio Bolsonaro as the candidate capable of delivering it after years of what the supporter called left-wing economic mismanagement.Another supporter said she was drawn to his promises to curb violence, tackle terrorism and drug trafficking, and bring down interest rates.Lula rallies supporters around national sovereigntyFollowing Bolsonaro's first-round lead, Lula's supporters have organised large rallies in an effort to mobilise voters and increase turnout. Around 33 million people did not vote in the first round earlier this month.Addressing a large gathering on Rio de Janeiro's Copacabana beach on Saturday, Lula framed the election as a question of national sovereignty. He said voters would have to choose between a leader who embraced Brazil's flag and one who embraced the American flag.Lula's government has accused the United States of interfering in Brazil's election, a charge Washington has dismissed as “baseless”.“We're going to win the election for one simple reason: it's true that the people want change [but] they want to move forward,” Lula told the crowd. “They don't want to go backward.”A Lula supporter, Roberta, told BBC News that the rallies were intended to demonstrate the movement's strength and encourage people to take to the streets to help reverse the first-round result.Another supporter, wearing Brazil's iconic yellow and green football shirt, said Bolsonaro's supporters had “appropriated” the national jersey, but Lula's backers were now reclaiming it.You use AI every day. articles.title: For 20 years, a former New Jersey military housing site sat abandoned; now a $70 million plan will replace the decaying complex with 275 homes and new shops near Netflix's planned $1 billion studio
articles.summary: For two decades, a stretch of Eatontown, New Jersey, stood as a reminder of a community left behind.
articles.body: For two decades, a stretch of Eatontown, New Jersey, stood as a reminder of a community left behind. Once home to military families, the abandoned Howard Commons site gradually deteriorated, its vacant buildings and neglected grounds becoming an eyesore along Pinebrook Road. Now, the long-neglected property is set for a dramatic transformation, with developers betting that new homes, shops and a nearby Netflix production campus could help usher in a new chapter for the region.According to reports by the New York Post and Realtordot com, developers have broken ground on The Premiere at Monmouth, a $70 million residential and retail development planned for the former military housing site. The project will bring 275 homes alongside a public park, grocery store, convenience store and gas station, creating a new neighbourhood as Eatontown prepares for a wave of investment and employment opportunities.From military housing to a new communityAccording to New York Post, Howard Commons was once part of the former Fort Monmouth military installation, providing housing for hundreds of military families. Following years of vacancy and deterioration, the property became a symbol of stalled redevelopment. The latest plan, developed through an agreement between the borough and Lennar Corp., aims to replace the decaying complex with a community designed around contemporary residential needs, the report adds.The new development is expected to include single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, catering to a range of prospective buyers, from first-time homeowners to families seeking additional space. The inclusion of everyday retail and public green space is intended to make the project more than a housing complex, giving residents access to essential services and shared outdoor areas, the New York report explains.As reported by Realtor dot com, Lennar has worked with the Fort Monmouth Economic Revitalization Authority since the early 2000s and identified the long-vacant site as an opportunity for redevelopment. The developer is now positioning the project as part of a broader revival of Monmouth County.Netflix's billion-dollar betA major factor behind the renewed interest in the area is Netflix's planned studio complex at Fort Monmouth. The streaming giant broke ground on its $1 billion Netflix Studios East project in 2025, transforming part of the former US Army installation into a major East Coast production hub, Realtor report explains.Scheduled to open in 2028, the 292-acre campus is expected to feature 12 sound stages covering nearly 500,000 square feet, alongside facilities supporting other production activities and community amenities. The project is anticipated to generate jobs and attract businesses serving the entertainment industry, strengthening the region's prospects as a growing centre for film and television production, adds the report by New York Post and Realtor too.The Premiere at Monmouth is about a 10-minute drive from the planned studio campus. Developers are hoping that proximity to the facility will appeal to buyers looking to live near future employment opportunities and the businesses expected to follow.The area's housing market has already shown signs of heightened demand. In May, NJ dot com reported that a five-bedroom home in nearby Little Silver sold for $2.6 million, approximately 24% above its $2.1 million asking price. articles.title: Gunmen kill at least 10 villagers and loot shops in northeast Nigeria
articles.summary: Police are searching for other casualties, with officials warning the actual death toll could rise further.
articles.body:
Unknown gunmen have raided a remote village in the northeast Nigerian state of Taraba, killing at least 10 people, looting shops and setting houses ablaze, police say.

There are fears the actual death toll is much higher, with eyewitnesses speaking of 20 lives lost and a non-governmental organisation suggesting a toll of as many as 50.

The gunmen reportedly swooped on the village of Binnari in the Karim Lamido area mounted on motorcycles just after midday Muslim prayers on Friday in a rampage that went on for up to four hours.

Police say they are searching for other casualties in the bush but the authorities were accused by Amnesty International of failing to protect rural communities.

Nigeria continues to face attacks by armed groups across several regions, including the northwest, northeast and central regions.

The country is also battling a jihadist insurgency in its northeast that has lasted nearly two decades, drawing persistent criticism of the government's handling of insecurity.

Following the latest incident, police said they recovered 10 bodies with gunshot wounds after officers responded to a distress call.

The attackers had fled by the time they arrived but they continued to patrol the area to restore calm, they told BBC News on Saturday.

"We were able to disperse the unknown gunmen though there was no casualty on their side and ours because the terrain is difficult and they're used to the terrain," Assistant Superintendent of Police Victor Mshelizah said.

He added that officers were continuing to search the bush nearby for people who might have been killed or wounded, and warned the death toll could still rise.

Speaking to AFP news agency, community leader Malam Abubakar Saifullahi said the attackers had arrived on about 50 motorcycles, two men apiece.

"They looted shops and took cash, foodstuffs and other provisions," he said. "They also took motorcycles abandoned by people fleeing the attack."

Survivors who spoke to AFP said they had counted at least 20 dead.

"People were running in different directions to escape the attack," Binnari resident Isiyaku Musa said. "Nobody knew where it was safe to go."

Another survivor, Sa'idu Nuhu, said that some people were still missing.

Amnesty's Nigeria director, Isa Sanusi, told BBC News on Saturday that the NGO had spoken to some of the bereaved families who said up to 50 people had died.

"The initial funeral had 37 people," he said.

Sanusi called for an impartial investigation into the killings, accusing the authorities of leaving rural communities "at the mercy of gunmen that are repeatedly commit atrocities with impunity".

articles.title: Cyclone Arnab to hit Andhra coast by October 28; heavy rain forecast in parts of Bengal
articles.summary: KOLKATA: The depression over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclone by Monday morning.
articles.body: KOLKATA: The depression over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal is likely to intensify into a cyclone by Monday morning. The cyclone, which will be called ‘Arnab’, is expected to hit the Andhra Pradesh coast by October 28 evening or earlier. Its impact is likely to bring rain to Kolkata and several districts of south Bengal from Tuesday, with heavy rain forecast in some areas between October 28 and 30, the Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) said.The system started as a low-pressure area over the east-central and adjoining south-east Bay of Bengal. It became a well-marked low-pressure area early on Saturday and developed into a depression later in the day. It is accompanied by a cyclonic circulation extending up to 5.8 km above sea level.Squally winds are expected along and off the Bengal coast from Tuesday. Kolkata is likely to receive light to moderate rain, while heavy rain has been forecast at one or two places in some districts of south Bengal between October 28 and 30.“The city will remain cloudy from Tuesday, while sporadic showers are expected over the subsequent three days. Since the cyclone will hit the Andhra coast on Wednesday, clouds from the outer band of the system will start floating into south Bengal from early on Tuesday. It will lead to clouds and trigger rain in the city and surrounding districts. In Kolkata, the rain frequency and intensity are likely to peak between Wednesday and Thursday. It may continue on Friday but will lose intensity as the cyclone hits land and starts moving towards central or eastern India,” said Sourish Bandopadhyay, weather scientist at the RMC.The cyclone is likely to hit the Andhra coast by October 28 evening or even earlier. “Squally winds and heavy rain are expected along the coasts of south Bengal with wind speed reaching 30-40 km/hour,” Bandopadhyay added.According to a special bulletin issued by the RMC on Saturday, light to moderate rain and thundershowers are expected at one or two places in East and West Midnapore, North and South 24 Parganas, Kolkata, Howrah and Hooghly on Tuesday. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are likely at one or two places in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore and Jhargram.Rain and thundershowers are expected to continue on October 28. Heavy rain of 70-110 mm is likely at some places in South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore and Jhargram. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also likely at several other places across south Bengal.On October 29, light to moderate rain is expected across south Bengal and Kolkata. Heavy rain has been forecast at some places in Midnapore, Bankura, Jhargram and Purulia. South 24 Parganas, East and West Midnapore are also likely to experience thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds during the day.The RMC has warned of possible lightning strikes in open fields between October 28 and 29. Waterlogging and some damage to standing crops are also possible.Kolkata remained dry and warm on Saturday, with the maximum temperature reaching 31.2°C. articles.title: Kate Winslet once dreamed of becoming a gardener but struggled to get started; from growing carrots and tomatoes to choosing the right soil and raised beds, here are 7 beginner-friendly ways to create a kitchen garden and grow fresh vegetables at home
articles.summary: Some people dream of a garden the way others dream of a holiday, and Kate Winslet is one of them.
articles.body: Some people dream of a garden the way others dream of a holiday, and Kate Winslet is one of them. When the Titanic star played French landscape designer Sabine De Barra in A Little Chaos, a period drama set in the gardens of Versailles under King Louis XIV, she got a taste of that life.According to WENN, she said, "every single night during filming I would go home and have to dig out mud." The film was directed by her friend Alan Rickman, who also played the king.On the contrary, in real life it is different, and she admits, "I don't have any gardening talents, truth be told. I'm just not very good at it, but I love gardens, and I'd love to be a gardener," she added. At the London premiere, she said according to an AFP report, she said "Every year I say 'Right, this year we're going to do raised beds, this year we're going to grow carrots, this year we're going to do tomatoes,' and somehow life gets in the way and we never get around to it."This feeling is common among us when we really want to begin learning gardening but do not know where to begin, but honestly, it is not that difficult. Here are seven easy ways to start a kitchen garden.Find a sunny spot firstSunlight decides how well your vegetables grow, so plan out and make space for your green friends in the sunny corner of your balcony. Most vegetables and herbs grow best with at least 6 to 8 hours of sunlight, so it is best to line the pots in your balcony, terrace, or backyard in that spot throughout the day.Begin with growing smaller herbs and plantsBig plans can often disappoint beginners, as they need extensive care. So, it is best to begin with smaller herbs like coriander, microgreens, and garlic and onion greens in pots or raised beds, especially avoiding plants that pests love.Get the soil rightGood soil does most of the work. Use raised bed soil in raised beds and potting mix in containers. Carrots need extra care, as they prefer loose, well-worked soil free of rocks, because a stone or hard clod can bend or split a growing root, so it is advised to remove stones before sowing.Give carrots room to growCarrots need patience to grow, for this begin by growing thin seedlings once they are about 3 inches tall so each root has room to grow, and to keep soil moist but not saturated, since overwatering may make carrots fork or crack.How to grow carrotsChoose a sunny spot with 6 to 8 hours of light. Plant seedlings once the soil is warm, burying them a little deep. Add a stake or cage for support. Water regularly at the base, keeping soil moist. Feed with compost lightly, pick tomatoes when fully coloured, and enjoy the fresh taste.Water steadily and keep regular checksPlants need regular water, and the garden needs your time, so grow only what you can care for, or stick to easy herbs and sprouts. Plants need an inch of water weekly, but it is also important to check the soil first, as too much water can be harmful.Protest plants from pests and diseasesHealthy plants fight trouble better, so it is important to check them every few days. Look under leaves for bugs, and pick pests off by hand when you spot them. Water at the base, give plants room for airflow, and remove sick leaves as soon as possible. Keeping your garden tidy also helps stop problems from spreading.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ testGet the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Saif Ali Khan finally gets his missing Gowardhan ghee, and says 'Hum Gowardhan ghee ke baare mein baat nahi karenge. All right?' But the internet can’t keep calm!
articles.summary: The internet loves a good running joke, but few memes have taken on a life of their own quite like Saif Ali Khan’s missing tub of cooking fat.
articles.body: The internet loves a good running joke, but few memes have taken on a life of their own quite like Saif Ali Khan’s missing tub of cooking fat.If you’ve been anywhere near Indian social media over the past few weeks, you’ve probably seen the chaos surrounding the actor’s promised reward from his appearance on Kaun Banega Crorepati 18. After Saif casually mentioned on air that he never actually received the two-year supply of Gowardhan Ghee he won on the game show, the internet did what the internet does best: it turned a minor TV giveaway into a full-blown online movement.Now, it looks like the long national wait is officially over, and fans are celebrating like they just won a trophy.In a newly posted Instagram video, Saif decided to sit down for a quick Q&A session with his followers. But before taking a single question, he tried to set some firm ground rules. Gesturing to the camera, he laid down the law right out of the gate: “Okay guys, let’s do this. Hi. Before we start, there is one thing I’d like to say, okay? Hum Gowardhan ghee ke baare mein baat nahi karenge. All right?”Naturally, his followers paid zero attention to that boundary.Almost immediately, the comment section turned into a wall of ghee-related spam. Viewers completely ignored his attempts to steer the conversation toward normal topics like movies or daily routines. When one user popped in to ask if the "gauravshali bhandar" (the glorious stock) had finally been delivered, Saif let out a sigh and tried to dodge it. “Nahi bhai, like I said, let’s talk about something fun and nice. Ask me some good questions. You can ask me anything,” he insisted.When another commenter teased that the only reason he even made an Instagram account was to collect his free dairy product, Saif laughed it off. “Okay. I know you think that’s why I came, but nahi bhai. Main khud se aaya hoon,” he explained.Despite his best efforts to keep things serious, the comments kept rolling in fast. One follower suggested he give up "aura farming" in favor of actual dairy farming, while others begged for tips on how to score their own multi-year supply. Eventually, Saif just had to throw his hands up in defeat. “Oh my God! You guys are obsessed with this ghee, and this needs to stop, all right?” he burst out, thoroughly amused by how relentless everyone was being.What made the whole clip even funnier was the subtle background detail: several massive jars of the famous ghee were sitting right behind him on set. Top that off with a caption reading, “This is the moment we’ve all been waiting for…a lifetime supply!!!” and fans took it as an absolute, undeniable victory.The comment section erupted within minutes, with both fans and industry peers jumping in on the joke. The official Sony LIV account chimed in to call it a true “gouravshaali moment,” while musician Yashraj Mukhate dropped a quick “Ghee refill.” Actor Anjali Dinesh Anand took a slightly different angle, marvelling at how easily the Bollywood star handled the camera despite being relatively new to social media content: “How is he already so good at this? I’ve been here a decade and don’t know how to be so good at Instagram.”The real triumph, however, belonged to the fan page @gheeonsaifside - an account created specifically to track down the missing game show reward. They immediately posted a victory lap, declaring in all caps, “HUM JEET GAYE @saifalikhanpataudi! 2 saal ka gauravshali Gowardhan Ghee ka bhandar finally mil gaya hai!!”Others flooded the post with jokes about the sheer volume of product, with one user writing, “Ghee kabhi khatam nahi hoga!” while another gave props to the clever publicity work behind the clip, pointing out that the brand's marketing team deserved a massive bonus for pulling off such a viral moment.Whether the video was a genuine update or just a brilliant self-aware marketing skit, one thing is for sure: the internet’s favorite celebrity feud - Saif versus a missing contest prize, has finally been put to rest in the most entertaining way possible.Get the latest movie news, reviews, and celebrity updates.
